questions.stem:
(a) Explain the meaning of a limited liability company. [2 marks]
(b) State four procedures for forming a public limited company in Nigeria. [8 marks]
(c) State five causes of business failure. [5 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) a business organisation registered under company law, with a separate legal personality, owned by shareholders whose liability is limited to the amount unpaid on their shares
8 marks: (b) any four, 2 marks each: promoters prepare memorandum and articles of association; register with the Corporate Affairs Commission and pay fees; obtain certificate of incorporation; issue prospectus and raise capital; obtain certificate to commence business/allot shares
5 marks: (c) any five: poor management; inadequate capital; poor record keeping; bad location; stiff competition; poor market research; mixing personal and business funds; unfavourable government policy (1 mark each)
questions.explanation: A limited liability company is a registered legal entity whose owners' liability is limited. Formation: promoters prepare documents, register with the CAC, get the certificate of incorporation, issue a prospectus and allot shares. Causes of failure include poor management, inadequate capital, poor records, bad location and competition.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the meaning of motivation. [2 marks]
(b) Explain Maslow's hierarchy of needs. [10 marks]
(c) State three barriers to effective communication in an organisation. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) the process of stimulating people to act willingly towards achieving goals
2 marks: (b) physiological needs: food, water, shelter, clothing
2 marks: (b) safety needs: security, job security, protection from danger
2 marks: (b) social needs: belonging, friendship, acceptance
2 marks: (b) esteem needs: recognition, status, respect
2 marks: (b) self-actualisation: realising one's full potential; needs are satisfied in order from lowest to highest
3 marks: (c) any three: language/jargon; noise; poor listening; status differences; information overload; poor choice of medium; distance (1 mark each)
questions.explanation: Motivation stimulates willing effort. Maslow's needs rise from physiological, safety, social and esteem to self-actualisation; a satisfied need no longer motivates. Barriers to communication include language, noise, poor listening and status differences.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the meaning of a contract. [2 marks]
(b) State and explain five essential elements of a valid contract. [10 marks]
(c) State three ways by which a contract may be discharged. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) a legally binding agreement between two or more parties
10 marks: (b) any five, 2 marks each: offer; acceptance; consideration; intention to create legal relations; capacity of the parties; legality of object; consent freely given; certainty of terms
3 marks: (c) any three: performance; agreement; breach; frustration; lapse of time; operation of law (1 mark each)
questions.explanation: A contract is a legally enforceable agreement. Essentials: offer, acceptance, consideration, intention, capacity, legality and free consent. Discharge is by performance, agreement, breach, frustration or operation of law.

questions.stem:
(a) State five functions of the Central Bank of Nigeria. [10 marks]
(b) Name and explain one tool of monetary control used by a central bank. [3 marks]
(c) Name two types of bank accounts. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
10 marks: (a) any five, 2 marks each: issues currency; banker to the government; banker to other banks; lender of last resort; controls money supply/monetary policy; manages foreign reserves; supervises banks; manages public debt
3 marks: (b) any one tool with explanation: open market operations; cash reserve ratio; monetary policy rate; liquidity ratio; moral suasion; special deposits
2 marks: (c) any two: current account; savings account; fixed (time) deposit account; domiciliary account (1 mark each)
questions.explanation: The CBN issues currency, banks for government and banks, is lender of last resort, controls money supply, manages reserves and supervises banks. For example, open market operations involve buying or selling securities to change money supply. Accounts include current, savings and fixed deposit.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the meaning of human resource management. [2 marks]
(b) Outline the steps in the recruitment and selection process. [8 marks]
(c) Distinguish between on-the-job and off-the-job training. [3 marks]
(d) State one importance of performance appraisal. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) the management of people in an organisation, covering recruitment, training, rewards and welfare
8 marks: (b) any four steps in order, 2 marks each: identify the vacancy and do job analysis; advertise the post; receive applications and shortlist; test/interview candidates; check references and medicals; offer appointment and induction
3 marks: (c) on-the-job training is given at the workplace while working (e.g. coaching); off-the-job training is outside normal work (e.g. seminars, courses)
2 marks: (d) any one: identifies training needs; basis for promotion and rewards; gives feedback to staff
questions.explanation: HRM manages people. Recruitment: job analysis, advertising, shortlisting, interviewing, checking references, offering the job and induction. On-the-job training happens at work; off-the-job training happens elsewhere. Appraisal identifies training needs and guides promotion.

questions.stem:
Read the case study and answer the questions.
Blessing Okeke, 24, finished secondary school in Enugu and learned tailoring. With ₦300,000 of her savings and a ₦500,000 loan from her uncle she rented a shop near a busy market, bought two sewing machines and employed two apprentices. Her clothes became popular. However, she kept no records, used shop money for family expenses, and often missed delivery dates. After two years she could not repay her uncle and her customers began going elsewhere.
(a) Identify two sources of finance used by Blessing. [4 marks]
(b) Identify three reasons for the problems of the business. [6 marks]
(c) State three types of records Blessing should keep. [3 marks]
(d) Suggest four ways she can sustain the business. [8 marks]
(e) State two ways government can support small businesses like hers. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
4 marks: (a) personal savings; loan from relatives (2 marks each)
6 marks: (b) any three, 2 marks each: no record keeping; mixing personal and business funds; poor time management/missed deliveries; failure to repay debts
3 marks: (c) any three: cash book/sales records; purchases records; debtors and creditors records; orders and delivery records; wages records (1 mark each)
8 marks: (d) any four, 2 marks each: keep proper records; separate business and personal money; plan and meet delivery dates; improve customer service; save part of profit; seek training; repay loan on a schedule
4 marks: (e) any two, 2 marks each: soft loans/grants; training through SMEDAN and similar agencies; tax incentives; providing infrastructure; access to markets
questions.explanation: Finance came from savings and a family loan. Problems: no records, mixing personal and business money, missed deliveries and unpaid debt. She should keep sales, purchases and debtors records, separate funds, manage time and repay her loan. Government can give soft loans, training and infrastructure.
